title: AI Image Detection
shortDescription: AI-generated image detection and cross-generator evaluation for EECS 4080 at York University.
longDescription: EfficientNet-B3 detector for AI-generated images, evaluated for calibration and for whether high scores were reading generator fingerprints or resampling artifacts.
challenge: A detector can look strong on a standard cross-generator test and still be scoring compression and resolution artifacts instead of generator fingerprints.
solution: Fine-tuned EfficientNet-B3 on 120,000 images, then measured calibration, swept the decision threshold, and ran a resolution-matched control plus FFT, t-SNE, and Grad-CAM on the hardest generators.
outcome: 96.96% test accuracy and 0.9971 AUC-ROC. Temperature scaling brought expected calibration error to 0.0026. The control showed matched-resolution detection fell to 35–62%, so the earlier cross-generator scores were not a clean generator fingerprint.

title: FinRAG AI
shortDescription: Financial question answering grounded in SEC filings and earnings data.
longDescription: Retrieval-augmented generation for financial Q&A, using hybrid search over filings and transcripts plus FinBERT sentiment.
challenge: Naive chunking split answers across boundaries and returned confident, incomplete facts.
solution: Hybrid BM25 and FAISS retrieval with a cross-encoder reranker, all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings, FinBERT for sentiment, and GPT-3.5-Turbo for generation. A local FAISS index keeps the retrieval layer under version control, and GitHub Actions runs the tests.
outcome: Retuning chunk overlap and relevance scoring lifted context recall to 0.92 on the hybrid-plus-rerank configuration.

title: MedRisk ML
shortDescription: 30-day hospital readmission risk for diabetic patients, with an explanation on every prediction.
longDescription: End-to-end clinical model for 30-day readmission, served through FastAPI and Streamlit with SHAP explanations and MLflow tracking.
challenge: A risk score is not useful to a clinician unless the service can say why one patient was flagged and another was not.
solution: Trained XGBoost and LightGBM on 100K+ records and 30+ engineered clinical features, tracked experiments in MLflow, and attached per-prediction SHAP explanations inside the FastAPI service. Docker packages the stack.
outcome: 0.87 ROC-AUC after cross-validated tuning, with the winning model registered in MLflow.

title: ML Engineer Skills
shortDescription: A checker for common ML mistakes: leakage, broken splits, unbeaten baselines, and metric misuse.
longDescription: Open-source checks that flag data leakage, broken train-test splits, baselines that were never beaten, and metrics used in the wrong setting. Run the mlcheck tool, or use the Claude Code skills.
challenge: Models get reported before anyone checks whether the split leaked, the baseline was beaten, or the metric matches the decision.
solution: Packaged those checks as the mlcheck tool and as Claude Code skills so the same review can run in a script or inside an agent workflow.
outcome: A reusable review step for ML experiments, published as a public repository.

title: Permit Wait
shortDescription: Calibrated wait-time estimates for Toronto building permits.
longDescription: Estimates how long a Toronto building permit is likely to take, with calibration so the stated wait is not just a point prediction.
challenge: A permit wait time is only useful if the stated range is something an applicant can trust.
solution: Built a Python model that estimates Toronto building-permit wait times and checks that those estimates are calibrated.
outcome: A public estimator focused on calibrated wait times rather than an uncalibrated point forecast.

title: Toronto AI/ML Internship Radar
shortDescription: Live feed of Winter 2027 AI/ML internships and co-ops in Canada, refreshed by GitHub Actions.
longDescription: A public feed of Canadian AI and ML internships and co-ops, rescraped on a schedule with no paid APIs.
challenge: Internship boards go stale, and a filter that is too strict drops postings a student would still want to see.
solution: GitHub Actions refreshes the feed about every 10 minutes. Classification rules filter by region, recency, and hiring cycle, and keep ambiguous postings rather than dropping them.
outcome: A live Winter 2027 feed of AI/ML internships and co-ops in Canada.

title: Realtime Face Recognition
shortDescription: OpenCV LBPH face recognition on a live webcam feed, with a Streamlit demo.
longDescription: Trains a local LBPH recognizer on a small set of face images and identifies those people in a webcam stream. All processing stays on the machine.
challenge: A face recognizer has to train on a handful of photos and still run smoothly on a laptop webcam.
solution: OpenCV's LBPH recognizer, a capture-and-train flow, and a Streamlit app for browser-camera training and recognition.
outcome: A local real-time recognizer with a public Streamlit demo.
